title: Investigation into the influence of an exergame and/or VR-based Back training to reduce pain and mobility for chronic back pain in a rehabilitation setting
summary: Chronic back pain is one of the most common reasons for inability to work. Exercise is considered an effective treatment. This study investigates whether a new type of computer-assisted training ("exergaming") on a moving device (ICAROS Health) is more effective than standard therapy. On this device, patients perform playful holding exercises ("planking") by shifting their weight to control a video game. In some cases, virtual reality goggles are worn. Patients in inpatient rehabilitation are being studied. One group trains additionally on the device for three to four weeks, while the other group receives conventional treatments such as physiotherapy and back school. The aim is to find out whether pain, core strength, and flexibility can be improved more effectively through playful training.
conditions: Individuals with chronic back pain not attributable, upon medical examination, to acute disc herniation, sudden and severe inflammation, vertebral fracture, osteoporosis, tumor, or acute trauma.

interventions.name: A regular 3-to-4-week inpatient rehabilitation program for chronic back pain, supplemented by 4 sessions of ICAROS Health per week (20–30 minutes per session).
3-to-4-week standard inpatient rehabilitation program for chronic back pain

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Rehabilitation patients with chronic non-specific back pain (medical diagnosis).
Exclusion criteria:
Acute disc herniation, sudden or severe inflammation, vertebral fracture, osteoporosis, tumor, acute trauma.
